title: 美国市中心转型：写字楼空置催生居住新需求
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: This was one of the most famous office buildings in America.
segments.zh: 这曾是全美最著名的办公楼之一。

segments.en: Now it has gone residential, with condo buyers starting to move in.
segments.zh: 如今它已改为住宅，公寓买家开始入住。

segments.en: Office to residential conversions have been happening here in New York City for decades, in some other American cities too, but the pandemic and the accompanying turn to remote work
segments.zh: 办公楼改住宅在纽约已进行数十年，美国其他城市也有，但疫情及随之而来的远程办公

segments.en: have added new urgency to the task of repopulating America's downtowns.
segments.zh: 给美国市中心重新聚集人口的任务增添了新的紧迫性。

segments.en: Urban office prices have plummeted, posing challenges for city budgets dependent on commercial real estate taxes.
segments.zh: 城市办公楼估值大幅下滑，给依赖商业地产税的城市预算带来挑战。

segments.en: The concept of downtown as a place for stores, offices, and other businesses, but not homes originated here in New York City.
segments.zh: 市中心作为商店、办公室和其他商业场所而非住宅区的概念，起源于纽约。

segments.en: As people moved out of downtown, shops, cultural institutions, and eventually offices moved out too.
segments.zh: 随着人们搬离市中心，商店、文化机构乃至办公室也相继迁出。

segments.en: There's now more office space in American suburbs than in central business districts.
segments.zh: 如今美国郊区的办公空间已超过中央商务区。

segments.en: Downtowns do still have more high quality office space, and in New York rents at the very high end are hitting new records.
segments.zh: 市中心仍拥有更多优质办公空间，纽约顶级写字楼租金正创新高。

segments.en: There's not much demand, though, for offices in old quirky buildings like this one.
segments.zh: 然而，对这类老旧奇特建筑中办公楼的需求并不大。

segments.en: On the plus side, that lowers the economic hurdles for conversion to residential and other uses.
segments.zh: 有利的一面是，这降低了改造成住宅及其他用途的经济门槛。

segments.en: That's exactly what downtowns need to thrive again, to return to a past when people lived alongside offices and shops.
segments.zh: 这正是市中心再次繁荣所需要的，回归人们与办公室和商店比邻而居的过去。

segments.en: New York City's old downtown, now known as the financial district, started this process in the 1980s.
segments.zh: 纽约市的老市中心，现称为金融区，在20世纪80年代开始了这一进程。

segments.en: Its population has gone from less than a thousand to more than 60,000, and growing. In some other US cities, it's still a stretch to think of downtown
segments.zh: 其人口从不到一千增长到六万多，且仍在增长。在美国其他一些城市，还很难想象市中心

segments.en: as an appealing place to live or hang out rather than just work.
segments.zh: 是一个吸引人居住或闲逛的地方，而不仅仅是工作场所。
